# Find machine name in Ubuntu (2025-10-22 11:04Z)

_**User (2025-10-21 07:48Z)**_

What is the command to find a machine's name on ubuntu?

---

_**Agent (model default, mode Agent)**_

The command to find a machine's name on Ubuntu is:

```bash
hostname
```

This will display the hostname of the current machine.

You can also use these related commands:

- `hostname -f` - displays the fully qualified domain name (FQDN)
- `hostname -s` - displays the short hostname
- `hostname -i` - displays the IP address of the hostname
- `cat /etc/hostname` - shows the hostname stored in the system configuration file

The `hostname` command is the most common and straightforward way to get the machine's name on Ubuntu and other Linux distributions.

_**User (2025-10-21 07:48Z)**_

What is the difference between ";" and "&&" between shell commands?

---

_**Agent (model default, mode Agent)**_

Great question! The difference between `;` and `&&` in shell commands is about how they handle command failures:

## `;` (Semicolon) - Sequential Execution
- Commands separated by `;` run **sequentially regardless of success or failure**
- Each command runs independently
- If one command fails, the next command still runs
- Example: `command1; command2; command3`

## `&&` (Double Ampersand) - Conditional Execution  
- Commands separated by `&&` run **only if the previous command succeeded**
- If any command fails (non-zero exit code), execution stops
- This is "short-circuit" evaluation
- Example: `command1 && command2 && command3`

## Examples:

```bash
# With semicolon - all commands run regardless of failures
false; echo "This will print"; echo "This will also print"

# With && - stops at first failure
false && echo "This won't print" && echo "This won't print either"
true && echo "This will print" && echo "This will also print"
```

## In Your Makefile Context:

```makefile
# Current version - git pull runs even if cd fails
cd /home/air/temperaturebot; git pull

# Safer version - git pull only runs if cd succeeds
cd /home/air/temperaturebot && git pull
```

For your `deploy` target, you might want to use `&&` to ensure `git pull` only runs if the directory change succeeds:

```makefile
deploy:
	@if [ "$$(hostname)" = "slg1" ]; then \
		cd /home/air/temperaturebot && git pull; \
	else \
		echo "Deploy skipped: not running on slg1 (current hostname: $$(hostname))"; \
	fi
```

This way, if the directory doesn't exist or you don't have permission, `git pull` won't run in the wrong location.
